goal: Maximize monthly outbound clicks from workagedleads.com to agedleadstore.com

baseline.note: Prior figure excludes a 73-session spike on 2026-07-07; including it the prior rate is 16.5/day. Post-cutover decline is real and independently reproduces the 5.6/day figure in the email plan.

milestone.rationale: Recover to the pre-cutover rate. First milestone, not the ceiling.

iterations.notes: Per-page affiliate attribution added to /api/reports/outbound-clicks (affiliate.byPage30d, clickRate, leakage). Ledger created. scripts/price-index-gap.ts generates the Q3 study brief. Newsletter restart was found already complete and running — the 2026-08-10 issue sent 2026-08-12 as broadcast a830c99a.

expected.basis: No prior estimate possible — the page had zero affiliate links, so its C was structurally 0 and any traffic it earned converted at 0. This is a wiring fix, not a demand bet. First real expected-value scores start at iteration 2, once affiliate.byPage30d has data.

at2w.note: Neither after-pricing nor after-economics appears in GA4 at all. Verified this is real absence and not a key mismatch: app/(site)/blog/aged-lead-industry-statistics/page.tsx:227 passes content="after-pricing" and :563 passes affiliateContent="after-economics", so the values would have been emitted had anyone clicked.

iterations.notes: Site's most-cited asset (CiteThisButton, Dataset JSON-LD, CC-licensed) had no route to a purchase — every outbound link was internal. Added InlineTextCta after the pricing tables and a compact CtaBanner after the economics section. Two placements not three: a reference page that reads as a sales pitch stops being cited. UTM content values after-pricing / after-economics distinguish the placements. Verified in built HTML; destination returns 200 with a browser UA (bot-blocked for curl default). Page's lastUpdated is still 2026-04-08 — that is the Q3 study's job, not this one. MEASURED 2026-09-01: zero sessions from both placements in 13 days. The page earns citations, not purchases — its readers are researchers looking for a number to quote, not buyers. Do not add a third placement; the constraint is audience intent, not CTA count.

iterations.targetCluster: commercial lead-type queries (aged mortgage leads, aged insurance leads, final expense leads, iul leads)

expected.basis: 629 views/mo across the top four lead-type pages converting at ~0.95% today. Modelling C at 5% — 8x below the provider page's measured 43.33% — gives ~31 clicks vs 6, i.e. +25/mo on a 69-click base. A hypothesis to test, not a forecast: intent on a guide page is genuinely lower than on a provider review, and the gap will not fully close.

at2w.note: hero-door took 41 of 54 post-window affiliate sessions, but the three placements it sits above fell from 46 to 6. Net movement is +5 sessions over 13 days (~+11/mo) against a predicted +25/mo. This is REDISTRIBUTION, not creation: the door captures the click higher on the page rather than producing an additional one.
at2w.limit: Site-side GA4 (528489903) still returns 403 to this service account, so lead-type pageviews - the denominator - could not be read. If site traffic FELL in the post window (plausible mid-crawl-transition), the same clicks from fewer visitors would be a genuine click-rate gain. Direction is unknown, so the 5% conversion hypothesis is neither confirmed nor refuted. Resolving the 403 is what makes iteration 2 conclusively measurable.

iterations.notes: Both hero buttons on these pages were internal (/compare, /price-index), so the site's highest-traffic commercial pages had no affiliate path above the fold. The mid-page CtaBanner also passes buttonHref, which sets useAffiliate=false — it is an internal compare link sitting exactly where intent peaks. Added a deep-linked door as the primary hero action; compare and pricing keep their position as secondary. Deep links verified per page: mortgage-leads -> /mortgage-leads-purchase-refinance/, final-expense-leads -> /life-insurance-leads/. insurance-leads correctly falls back to /all-lead-types/ — the partner has no generic-insurance buy page and that mapping is deliberate (lib/affiliate.ts, confirmed by Bill 2026-08-06). Destinations re-verified: 200, zero redirects, real buy pages ('Aged Mortgage Leads', 'Buy Aged Life Insurance Leads for Agents — From $0.25'). rel=nofollow sponsored and disclosure present on every instance. Measure via utm_content=hero-door. MEASURED 2026-09-01: keep the door (earlier capture is strictly safer than a buried CTA, and it costs nothing), but do NOT roll this pattern onto more pages expecting +25/mo each. The read across iterations 1 and 2 together is that this site's binding constraint is D, not C - more doors mostly reshuffle the same clicks. Spend the next iterations on creating visitors, not re-routing them.

scoreboardReadings.note: First reading from the per-page attribution built in iteration 0. Affiliate daily average of 2.30 is BELOW the 3/day flag threshold in CLICK-LOOP.md — but this counts GA4 outbound click events, while the 5.4/day baseline counts sessions arriving at agedleadstore.com. Different denominators; do not read one as a decline against the other. Trend this series against itself going forward.

scoreboardReadings.source: GA4 357329146 (store-side sessions, NOT the site-side click events in the 2026-08-18 reading - different denominators, do not compare the two series)
scoreboardReadings.note: 4.15/day against a 15/day milestone. Newsletter contribution in this window was ZERO (workagedleads/email = 0 sessions post vs 16 pre) - the list has been dark since the 2026-08-12 send, so the entire measured figure comes from organic site traffic alone.

nextPick.candidate: Weekly newsletter on the three-CTA template (shipped fc11fa2, unsent)
nextPick.rationale: Iterations 1 and 2 both tested conversion (C) on existing traffic. Iteration 1 returned zero; iteration 2 returned +5 sessions net and mostly moved clicks around. Two independent reads say C is not where the headroom is - D is. Email is the only lever that creates visitors without waiting on the stalled crawl: the single 2026-08-12 send produced 17 sessions, and workagedleads/email measured exactly 0 in this window because nothing was mailed. The template now carries 12 store links against 9 site links with the first at 20% page depth.

expected.basis: 17 sessions on the old one-link template x 4.3 sends/mo = 74/mo at parity, before any lift from the CTA rebuild. That alone would roughly double the 4.15/day site figure. Treat 17/send as the floor, since it was measured on a template with a single store link at 79% page depth.

alsoConsidered: Resolving the 528489903 GA4 403. Not an iteration - it produces no clicks - but it is the reason iteration 2's verdict has to stay 'partial'. Every future C-side experiment is unmeasurable without it.
Rolling hero-door onto more page types. Explicitly NOT recommended on this evidence: the measured effect was redistribution, so replicating it would buy far less than the +25/mo the model assumed.
Leakage recapture (61 of 130 outbound clicks). Unchanged from iteration 2's assessment, and still off-limits as removal - those links are what make the reviews independent.

kills.reason: Zero sessions from after-pricing and after-economics in 13 days. Killing the BET, not the code: the two placements stay (they cost nothing and do not harm citation value), but the statistics page is retired as a monetization target. Its readers want a number to quote, not leads to buy.
